Match: "content":"I have resolved the issue where clicking the onboarding button appeared to do nothing.\n\n### Why This Happened\n1. **Redirect Race Condition**: When you clicked the button, the URL transitioned to `/onboarding/consent`. The page started loading, which fired the async backend auth query. However, because React state changes are batched, `App.jsx` rendered once before the loading flag was updated. During this render, the protective redirect engine saw that `user` was still `null` in the local state, so it instantly redirected you back to `/auth` in the background (within a single frame, preventing the onboarding page from painting).\n2. **Local Cookie Rejections**: In local HTTP testing using an IP address (like `127.0.0.1:3000`), modern browsers reject secure cookies prefixed with `__Host-` because it is not an HTTPS context. This caused the session cookies to get dropped, rendering you unauthenticated on the next API call and sending you back to the login screen.\n\n### How it is Fixed\n1. **Synchronous Auth Reset**: I updated `App.jsx` to immediately set `authChecked` to `false` *synchronously* as soon as route changes occur. This blocks the redirect engine from running any premature redirects until the asynchronous `/api/auth/me` request has fully loaded and updated the state.\n2. **Dynamic Cookie Resolver (`src/utils/cookies.ts`)**:\n   - Created a dynamic cookie configuration helper.\n   - **Production & Tests**: Continues to use secure `__Host-iw-access` and `__Host-iw-refresh` cookies.\n   - **Development**: Seamlessly switches to standard HTTP cookies (`iw-access`, `iw-refresh`) without the `Secure` flag. This allows you to test on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or local network IPs over plain HTTP without the browser rejecting the cookies.\n\nAll 16 lifecycle tests and Next.js production builds have completed and **passed successfully**. File: transcript.jsonl
Match: "content":"I have resolved the Redis connection error spam issue by implementing a production-grade reconnection strategy and error throttling in the configuration.\n\n### What Caused the Issue?\nWhen the Redis Docker container or local instance was not running (or was booting up), `IORedis` default behavior would try to reconnect in a tight loop and emit an `error` event for every single failure. This flooded your console logs with repeating `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379` errors, causing massive logs, CPU waste, and hiding other messages.\n\n### How I Fixed It:\nI modified the configuration in [config.ts](file:///d:/Internship/Ingress%20Within/src/lib/queue/config.ts):\n1. **Exponential Reconnect Backoff**: Added a `retryStrategy` where the delay increases with every failure (`times * 500ms`), capping at **10 seconds** between reconnection attempts.\n2. **Log Throttling**: Connection error logs are now throttled to at most **once every 30 seconds**. This prevents console flooding while keeping you informed of the status.\n3. **Status Log Transitions**: Added status tracking for `connect`, `ready`, and `close` states, so it logs a single warning when the connection closes and prints a success confirmation once re-established."

It covers two signal types: immediate crisis (single entry) and sustained distress (pattern over time). For both, the platform stays active and present — it does not suspend or restrict access. The response is to change what is offered, not to withdraw.\r\n5: \r\n6: --- TABLE ---\r\n7: ⚠ Account suspension was considered and rejected. The BullMQ Workers will process these jobs asynchronously, execute the appropriate AI provider tasks, and write results back to the database.\n10: \n11: ```\n12: User Action ──> Save Data ──> Create Queue Job ──> Return HTTP 201/200\n13:                                        │\n14:                                        ▼ (Redis Queue)\n15:                               [BullMQ Worker Daemon]\n16:                                        │\n17:                                        ▼\n18:                               Execute AI/Logic Pass\n19:                                        │\n20:                                        ▼\n21:                               Store Result to Supabase\n22: ```\n23: \n24: ---\n25: \n26: ## 🛠️ Proposed Queues & Jobs\n27: \n28: We will register the following seven BullMQ queues:\n29: \n30: 1. **`entry_scoring`**: Runs after entry save; scans entry content for crisis signals (self-harm, severe distress) and flags accounts.\n37: \n38: ---\n39: \n40: ## ⚙️ Queue Configuration & Retry Strategy\n41: \n42: * **Retry Delay**: 1 minute, 5 minutes, 15 minutes.\n43: * **Dead Letter Queue (DLQ)**: If a job fails after 3 retry attempts, it will transition to the `failed` state in BullMQ, which acts as our DLQ. We will build a monitoring utility to inspect and retry failed jobs.\n44: * **BullMQ Custom Backoff Strategy**:\n45:   ```typescript\n46:   settings: {\n47:     backoffStrategies: {\n48:       custom(attemptsMade: number) {\n49:         const delays = [60000, 300000, 900000]; // 1m, 5m, 15m in ms\n50:         return delays[attemptsMade - 1] || -1; // -1 stops retrying\n51:       }\n52:     }\n53:   }\n54:   ```\n55: \n56: ---\n57: \n58: ## 📂 Directory & Folder Structure\n59: \n60: All background processing files will reside under `src/lib/queue/`:\n61: \n62: * **`src/lib/queue/config.ts`**: Redis connections, queue options, and custom backoff strategy.\n63: * **`src/lib/queue/registry.ts`**: Registry class to manage Queue instantiations and job submission helpers.\n64: * **`src/lib/queue/workerRegistry.ts`**: Registers and instantiates workers for all queues.\n65: * **`src/lib/queue/monitoring.ts`**: Dashboard/health metrics to count jobs (active, completed, failed/DLQ, delayed).\n66: * **`src/lib/queue/run-worker.ts`**: Entry point executable script to run the worker daemon process.\n67: * **`src/lib/queue/workers/`**: Contains worker-specific handler logic:\n68:   * `entryScoringWorker.ts`\n69:   * `reflectionWorker.ts`\n70:   * `weeklySummaryWorker.ts`\n71:   * `monthlyReportWorker.ts`\n72:   * `oceanSummaryWorker.ts`\n73:   * `exerciseInsightWorker.ts`\n74:   * `crisisDetectionWorker.ts`\n75: \n76: ---\n77: \n78: ## 🔧 AI Provider Extensions\n79: \n80: We will extend `AIProvider` and its implementations (`ClaudeProvider`, `GroqProvider`) to add:\n81: * `detectCrisis(content: string): Promise<{ isCrisis: boolean; reason?: string }>`\n82: \n83: This keeps crisis evaluation aligned with the AI provider structure.\n84: \n85: ---\n86: \n87: ## 🧪 Verification Plan\n88: \n89: ### Automated Verification\n90: We will write a verification script `scratch/test-queues.ts` to:\n91: 1. This flooded your console logs with repeating `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379` errors, causing massive logs, CPU waste, and hiding other messages.\n\n### How I Fixed It:\nI modified the configuration in [config.ts](file:///d:/Internship/Ingress%20Within/src/lib/queue/config.ts):\n1. **Exponential Reconnect Backoff**: Added a `retryStrategy` where the delay increases with every failure (`times * 500ms`), capping at **10 seconds** between reconnection attempts.\n2. **Log Throttling**: Connection error logs are now throttled to at most **once every 30 seconds**. This prevents console flooding while keeping you informed of the status.\n3. **Status Log Transitions**: Added status tracking for `connect`, `ready`, and `close` states, so it logs a single warning when the connection closes and prints a success confirmation once re-established."

Don’t want to talk about it.”\r\n442: -------------\r\n443: \r\n444: \r\n445: \r\n446: --- TABLE ---\r\n447: Dimension | Score | Reasoning\r\n448: EI | 5 | “Rough” implies something but gives no signal of intensity. Midpoint. Flag: limited signal.\r\n449: PR | 5 | No data. Midpoint. Flag: limited signal.\r\n450: SA | 5 | No data. Midpoint. Flag: limited signal.\r\n451: -------------\r\n452: \r\n453: \r\n454: Key teaching point: A short avoidant entry is not the same as a neutral entry. The refusal to elaborate is data — but it is not scoreable data. Score all three dimensions toward midpoint and flag explicitly. If this pattern persists across multiple entries, flag for attention in the monthly report. Consistent avoidance of elaboration is itself a signal worth naming.\r\n455: \r\n456: \r\n457: \r\n458: --- TABLE ---\r\n459: Scenario 7 — Reflection-Only Day\r\n460: -------------\r\n461: \r\n462: \r\n463: Profile: Processed retrospective content, no new entry\r\n464: \r\n465: --- TABLE ---\r\n466: “Looking back at yesterday — I think I was harder on myself than the situation warranted. The mistake wasn’t that big. I tend to catastrophise when I’m tired and I was very tired. I can see that now. I’ll try to catch it earlier next time.”\r\n467: -------------\r\n468: \r\n469: \r\n470: \r\n471: --- TABLE ---\r\n472: Dimension | Score | Reasoning\r\n473: EI | 3 | Processed content. Emotional charge of yesterday has passed. “Harder on myself” and “catastrophise” suggest the original event was higher EI but this writing is analytical. Score the writing not the event. 25% weight applied as reflection-only day.\r\n474: PR | 3 | “I tend to catastrophise when I’m tired” — pattern awareness with a specific condition attached. Not universal (“I always catastrophise”) — contextualised to tiredness. Low-mid PR. The conditionality is a flexibility signal.\r\n475: SA | 8 | “I can see that now.” “I’ll try to catch it earlier next time.” Retrospective ownership is high. Reflections often score higher SA — looking back and assigning agency is the nature of reflection. This is expected and is why the 25/75 weighting exists.\r\n476: -------------\r\n477: \r\n478: \r\n479: Key teaching point: Reflections will almost always score lower EI and higher SA than same-day entries. This is expected — the 25–75 weighting accounts for it. Do not adjust the anchor descriptions for reflections. Score them on the same scale and let the weighting do its job. Score the writing not the event being described.\r\n480: \r\n481: \r\n482: \r\n483: --- TABLE ---\r\n484: Scenario 8 — The Key Misread: Self-Criticism vs Self-Agency\r\n485: -------------\r\n486: \r\n487: \r\n488: Profile: Entry that looks like high SA but is actually low SA and high PR\r\n489: \r\n490: --- TABLE ---\r\n491: “I’ve been really hard on myself today. I just keep thinking about what I said and how stupid it was. I’m so disappointed in myself. I can’t believe I said that. It was such a stupid thing to do. I just hate that about myself — I always say the wrong thing in those situations. I’m so frustrated with myself.”\r\n492: -------------\r\n493: \r\n494: \r\n495: \r\n496: --- TABLE ---\r\n497: Dimension | Score | Reasoning\r\n498: EI | 7 | “So disappointed.” “Hate.” “So frustrated.” Strong emotion language directed inward. Real intensity. Repeated emotional statements indicate flooding.\r\n499: PR | 8 | “I always say the wrong thing in those situations” — fixed universal pattern applied without question. “I hate that about myself” — closed verdict, not open examination. No alternative framing anywhere. No genuine question raised. Cycling on a predetermined conclusion about the self.\r\n500: SA | 2 | Despite being entirely about the self, this entry has very low SA. No choice examined. No role understood. No intention named. “I always say the wrong thing” is passivity toward a fixed pattern, not ownership of a specific choice. The person is not authoring their experience — they are being punished by a story about themselves.\r\n501: -------------\r\n502: \r\n503: \r\n504: \r\n505: --- TABLE ---\r\n506: ⚠ CRITICAL MISREAD: Self-criticism is not self-agency. An entry full of “I” statements and self-directed language can still score low SA if the language is punitive and pattern-locked rather than reflective and choice-aware. The test: is this person examining their choices, or being attacked by a fixed story about themselves?\r\n507: -------------\r\n508: \r\n509: \r\n510: Key teaching point: This is the most important misread in the entire rubric. The surface features (self-focus, first-person language, emotional intensity) all look like high SA. But the structure reveals low SA and high PR. Always score the structure of thinking, not the surface features of the writing.\r\n511: \r\n512: \r\n513: Deferred to v2\r\n514: The following refinements were identified but not included in v1 of this rubric:\r\n515: \r\n516: •  Dimension-specific entry weighting: PR and SA may warrant closer to 50/50 weighting between reflection and new entry. PR patterns show equally in retrospective and immediate writing. SA language is often more visible in reflections. Deferred because a single weighting is simpler to build and the accuracy gain does not justify v1 complexity.\r\n517: •  Confidence scoring: a formal confidence field (1–5) per dimension score, not just a flag. Would allow the averaging algorithm to weight high-confidence days more heavily than low-confidence ones. Requires additional field on the daily score record.\r\n518: •  Cross-entry PR detection: comparing framing across multiple entries to detect rigidity patterns that don’t appear in a single entry. Requires the AI to have access to prior entry scores or summaries when scoring the current day.\r\n519: \r\n520: \r\n521: End of Scoring Rubric v1\r\n522: \nThe above content does NOT show the entire file contents. If you need to view any lines of the file which were not shown to complete your task, call this tool again to view those lines.\n"
